Matt/Team — attaching my anchors in brief here (workbook to follow). Baseline assumption: $95,000/mo inference spend. Two commitment shapes: Accelerator (front-loaded discounts to win) and Flexible (smaller discounts, more carryover).

Accelerator (aim: win fast commit):
- 12 months: 7% platform discount + 12% support retainer reduction; one-time migration credit = 0.75x monthly baseline applied month 1; spike-bank carryover cap = 10% of bank for next month.
- 24 months: 12% platform discount + 18% retainer reduction; migration credit = 1.25x baseline; carryover cap = 20%.
- 36 months: 16% platform discount + 22% retainer reduction; migration credit = 2x baseline; carryover cap = 30% with quarterly reconciliation.

Flexible (aim: lower upfront commitment):
- 12 months: 4% discount; migration credit = 0.25x baseline; carryover cap = 15% for two months.
- 24 months: 8% discount; migration credit = 0.5x baseline; carryover cap = 20% for two months.

Spike-bank mechanics (summary):
- Customers pre-buy a monthly spike bank (tokens/compute hours) sized to expected peak.
- Drawdown rules: normal consumption consumes bank first; once exhausted, emergency overdraft is allowed up to 50% of the monthly bank once per quarter (auto-bill for overage).
- Carryover: unused bank can roll forward up to the carryover cap associated with the commitment shape.

Example (24m Accelerator): monthly baseline $95k, migration credit = $118.75k applied as invoice credit in month 1; effective first-month cash = $95k - $118.75k (credit applied) + retainer (if any). Workbook includes TCV and cashflow examples.

Marissa

Team 1Adding SLA matrix text and paging rules below. I kept it short for procurement; legal will tighten wording.

SLA matrix (operational summary):
- 99.8% (Core): P1 initial acknowledgement within 6 hours (8x5), P1 mitigation plan within 12 hours, on-call escalation to engineering manager after 24h unresolved. Service credit: 0.5% of monthly invoice per 4 hours of downtime beyond SLA, capped at 10% monthly.
- 99.95% (Elevated): P1 ack within 2 hours (8x5), P1 mitigation within 4 hours, on-call escalation to incident lead within 2 hours. Service credit: 1% of monthly invoice per 2 hours of downtime beyond SLA, capped at 25% monthly.
- 99.995% (High-Assurance): P1 page within 30 minutes (24x7), immediate incident lead involvement, full bridge within 1 hour. Service credit: 2% of monthly invoice per hour of downtime beyond SLA, capped at 50% monthly.

Paging rules / who gets called:
- Core: customer ops -> Redwood support -> engineering manager (if escalated).
- Elevated: customer ops -> Redwood 24x7 support -> incident lead.
- High-Assurance: direct page to designated on-call incident lead and named executive contact.

Fallback & Dedicated pools:
- Dedicated pools include documented migration window and runbook. If we need to fail to hosted fallback, latency targets relax but credits apply only if fallback exceeds 36 hours for Elevated and 24 hours for High-Assurance.

Credit calculation examples are in the attached SLA pack. I'll route final text to legal once we agree on the caps.

Naomi
